title: PS5’s Exciting New Zelda-Like Kena Game Just Got Delayed
description: Developer Ember Lab has announced that its upcoming PS5 game Kena: Scars of Kosmora, the sequel to 2021's much-loved Kena: Bridge of Spirits, has been delayed. The game--which gives off major Zelda vibes--was previously set to release this year, but now it's been delayed to 2027. In a blog post, the developers said they need more time to "deliver a top-notch game that exceeds the quality" of Bridge of Spirits. "Pushing our release into 2027 gives us the ability to really polish the expanded game experience we want to deliver," the studio said. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhgxkBxiCyg Scars of Kosmora is a linear adventure game, just like the 2021 entry, but the sequel has a "broader and deeper scope," the studio said. "We hope you’re just as excited to jump into Kena’s next adventure as we are to share it with you. We’ve been working hard to fill it with the wonder, charm, and challenge fans have come to expect," the team added. "We appreciate your patience and support as we take the time for Scars of Kosmora to be the evolution of Kena’s journey and experience we want to deliver." In Scars of Kosmora, main character Kena is now a seasoned spirit guide and embarks on a journey to the island of Kosmora to find a "cure for her affliction and to reconnect with a friend from her past." The island holds a "powerful corruption" that fractures her staff, so Kena adopts a new method of manipulating the elements to her advantage. "On her journey, Kena discovers and nurtures memorable spirit companions-- whose powers she will harness to solve puzzles and defeat enemies using new elemental abilities," reads a line from the game's description. 2021's Bridge of Spirits was released initially on PS4, PS5, and PC, and later came to Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S in 2024. A Switch 2 edition arrived in March this year. Kosmora has been confirmed only for PS5 and PC so far.

title: GTA 6’s Weather System Sounds Like A Big Step Up
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 includes a number of updates and improvements over the developer's past games, and that includes new weather systems. Rockstar's vice president of art for lighting and rendering at Rockstar, Owen Shepherd, told Game Informer that the studio has "re-engineered" the studio's weather system to "make everything more more localized and persistent." He said the goal was to make the weather in GTA 6's setting of Leonida--a stand-in for Florida--feel "dynamically solid and achieve a sense of scale" that the studio has never done before. GTA 6 launches on November 19.What that means in practice is that GTA 6 will have "fully dynamic cloudscapes that roll across the map" to provide a "broad spectrum of weather" in the game. Florida is known for its heat and humidity, along with its localized and fast-moving rain systems. Look one direction and you may see bright sunshine. Look the other and you could see a downpour. GTA 6 will replicate this with localized rain showers, along with rainbows that appear. Additionally, places where it recently rained in the game will remain wet, with puddles also popping up. GTA 6 also has a new wind system that includes "offshore breezes after sunset, convectional updrafts, and occlusion from buildings,” Shepherd said. “Hair and debris will swirl around on rooftops; gusts of wind will blow ripples over the water surface and bend the grass in swamps.” GTA 6 will also include tropical storms and hurricanes, along with thunder and lightning. Shepherd did not, however, get into how GTA 6's new weather systems could affect gameplay. Florida is known to experience devastating hurricanes, but it remains to be seen if, for example, a hurricane could knock down structures or trees. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, priced at $80 for its standard edition and $100 for the Ultimate Edition. Rockstar is also selling a $400 collector's edition that includes a bunch of physical goodies, but not the game.

title: Blizzard Isn’t Fixing Diablo 4 Season 15’s Biggest Bug
description: Diablo 4 Season 15's biggest bug, one revolving around Hellfire Torch and being able to equip more Unique charms than should be possible, won't be fixed this season, Blizzard has announced. Hellfire Torch is a new Unique charm that counts as an extra set charm and comes with some great beneficial stats, like +All Skills, +All Stats, and +All Resistances. Players can usually only have one Unique charm equipped at a time, but Hellfire Torch breaks that rule, allowing players to use it and another Unique charm. That's strong on its own, but there is currently a bugged interaction with Hellfire Torch that is allowing players to equip two Unique charms in addition to Hellfire Torch instead of one, granting even higher levels of power. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2L55dgNzpQ8 The bug seems to stem from Hellfire Torch being used first alongside the Seal of the Golden Epiphany, which allows players to equip up to three Unique charms. However, players are later swapping out Golden Epiphany for the Mythic Seal of the Diamond Mind, a seal that reduces the number of charms needed for set bonuses, but are still able to benefit from having additional Unique charms equipped. That, in turn, allows players to gain advantages from a full five-piece set bonus, Hellfire Torch, and two Unique charms all at once. Now, Diablo 4 design director Dan Tanguay in a forum post said Blizzard is aware of the bug and said Hellfire Torch' s current behavior is "beyond what was originally intended." That being said, Blizzard will be letting it ride this season as it works towards a fix in the future. "We know many players have spent significant time earning the Hellfire Torch and building characters around it," Tanguay said. "Because of that, we want to be thoughtful about making adjustments mid-season that could disrupt those investments." Tanguay continued: "We've also seen the positive reception to the Hellfire Torch itself from many players. The item has created a lot of excitement this season, and we've taken note of the feedback from those who have enjoyed earning it and incorporating it into their builds. While we don't have anything to announce today, it is something we're considering for the future, which makes it even more important that we fully understand and address this interaction the right way." The post states Blizzard will continue to investigate the issue so that any future changes will be "implemented correctly and behave as intended." Players in Season 15 just might be stronger than ever before. Alongside the bugged Hellfire Torch interaction, players can also use this trick to get around the game's crafted Mythic item restriction and fully deck themselves out in Mythic gear. It's just the last development in what has been one of Diablo 4's wildest, and most surprising, seasons yet. Season 15, Hell's Legacy, introduced all kinds of new content based on previous Diablo games, including boss fights against Diablo, Baal, and Mephisto ripped straight from earlier entries in the franchise. It's also filled to the brim with secrets upon secrets, including a showdown with the cow god Moophisto and even the return of the secret pony level, Whimsyshire, from Diablo 3. Diablo 4 will continue to receive new seasons going forward, but won't be getting new expansions, as Blizzard instead shifts its focus to Diablo 5. A new Diablo 4 class, the Amazon, will release as standalone DLC in the first half of 2027.

title: PS5 Just Got A PS5 Pro-Like AI Upgrade, But Don’t Expect It Everywhere Yet
description: The base PS5 console is no slouch when it comes to games, but compared to the PS5 Pro, it doesn't pack the same visual punch. That could change soon, as Sony has unveiled a new AI-upscaling upgrade for the older machine called Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR). Like PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), it is designed to make games look sharper and maximize performance. While PSSR will still remain the "gold standard" for what Sony games can look like on PS5 Pro, QSSR looks like it'll offer a noticeable improvement on PS5. A result of the AI graphics collaboration with AMD, Sony says that it offers a "streamlined neural network architecture" for games. The only catch? For now, only two PS5 games will support it: Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei--which is getting a new Complete Edition this month. Here are a few samples of it in action: https://youtu.be/RcFYsDKbAIk https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E929-XwrS_Q "QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments, bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan's epic journey. It’s a perfect companion to the launch of Marvel's Wolverine, and it brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience to our players on PS5," head of technology at Insomniac Games, Mike Fitzgerald, wrote in a PS Blog post. Jasmin Patry, lead rendering engineer at Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch Productions, added that QSSR excels at "resolving the fine details" in characters and environments that previously wasn't possible on the base PS5. Both PS5 exclusives are receiving a patch today to add QSSR as an additional graphics option, and Sony says it will be offered to all PlayStation developers soon. If it's implemented widely and across many more games, QSSR could become a big selling point for the PS5, as the console will be six years old in November. Price hikes have made it more expensive to jump into the current console generation, and for anyone who can afford the $900 PS5 Pro, stock seems increasingly harder to find as demand begins to outpace supply. In Japan, potential consumers are now being asked to enter a lottery system and prove they've played at least 60 hours over the last two years on their current PS5 console. In comparison, an improved gaming experience on a regular PS5 console sounds like it makes financial sense--even if the console was much cheaper when it first launched in 2020.

title: The Xbox Cloud Gaming Controller Is Dead, Apparently
description: Microsoft agreed to several big changes to appease regulators in its effort to get the blockbuster $75.4 billion deal to buy Activision Blizzard approved, including tweaks to its cloud-gaming projects. Now, more than a year later, we're still learning more about this, including a new claim from The New York Times that Microsoft canceled plans for a new Xbox controller "devoted to cloud gaming." A spokesperson for Microsoft denied that the controller concept was abandoned due to the regulatory process, but did not provide a reason. Microsoft never formally announced or unveiled any controller for cloud gaming, but an image of it leaked this year, prompting raised eyebrows for its ... unique design. Microsoft cut deals with a variety of companies--including Ubisoft, Nware, EE, Boosteroid, Ubitus, and Nvidia--to help mitigate concerns from the UK's Competition & Markets Authority (CMA) that Microsoft might give preferential treatment to its own cloud gaming networks. Former Xbox CEO Phil Spencer, who led Xbox during the sale process, said such deals freed up one of the concerns the CMA had and helped bring more games to more people. The Xbox cloud-gaming service showed some initial signs of growth, but the program suffered a setback recently when Microsoft announced that it will soon put limits on how much people can use the service, and then charge them more to keep playing. Additionally, Windows Central recently discovered that the dedicated cloud gaming app for older Samsung TVs will go away soon due to a compatibility issue. Access to cloud gaming is one of the perks of Xbox Game Pass Ultimate, allowing people to stream their games. Later this year, people will be able to buy game time for cloud gaming on Xbox without a Game Pass membership. One of the appeals of cloud gaming, at least in theory, is that it requires no expensive local hardware like an Xbox or PC, both of which are more expensive than ever due to the AI-fueled demand for memory and components. People need a consistent and fast internet connection for the best experience. In other Xbox news, CEO Asha Sharma recently stressed that Xbox is "not for sale," following rumors and reports that Microsoft could unload the struggling company.

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Clever Solution To One Of PC Gaming’s Biggest Annoyances
description: Early access for Gears of War: E-Day has kicked off for anyone who bought the Premium Edition, and if you're on PC, you're probably dreading the traditional shader compilation wait that comes with it. There's good news, as Gears of War: E-Day supports a neat feature on this platform that cuts down on that process significantly. Called Advanced Shader Delivery (ASD), it addresses how modern games rely on shaders to calculate how light, shadows, reflections, and textures should look on screen. This usually involves you sitting for a while when you first boot up a game after installing it, resulting in the infamous "Compiling Shaders" loading bar. In comparison, ASD is like buying a Gundam model kit that's already assembled, right out of the box. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xTxwN-Ck1Zw ASD pre-translates and delivers shader files directly to your device ahead of time, so you wait mere seconds. It also works across a wide variety of systems, and while I haven't installed Gears of War: E-Day on my main PC yet, I did load it up on my Asus Xbox ROG Ally X. The shader compilation waiting time was around 20 seconds, far better than waiting up to 15 minutes as I've experienced with other new games. It's also worth noting that ASD works with multiple hardware configurations, including devices powered by AMD, Intel, Nvidia, and Qualcomm. Gears of War: E-Day will be the first game to support ASD across Windows devices, and it's currently available for users with AMD graphics cards. Owners of Nvidia GPUs will receive ASD-compatible drivers shortly after E-Day launches. I was slaying the Locust, not my patience.While our impression of the multiplayer portion of Gears of War: E-Day is still coming, the campaign is a mostly solid excuse to take cover and pop some Locust heads. "For better or worse, E-Day is distinctly Gears, and I had a good time with it, even if the story is disappointing and the open areas are fairly dull," Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot's Gears of War: E-Day review. "But that’s all it is: a good game, propped up by combat that hasn’t changed all that much over the past 20 years. That’s enough to skate by, but I wish Gears of War would dig deeper."

title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Compromise Scale For Detail, Rockstar Says
description: Rockstar's games are known for their impressive attention to detail, along with their massive scopes, and GTA 6 is seemingly going to up the ante in that regard. Rockstar boss Aaron Garbut said in an interview that a developer might compromise scale for detail or detail for interaction "but not with this project." "We went the other way," he told Game Informer. "Everything is dialed up--detail, scope, breadth, scale, interaction, and density." He went on to say Rockstar has never "created anything close to this before." "As the pressure for us on this project is huge, we dealt with that by doing our best to overdeliver," Garbut said. Lucia and Jason in GTA 6.No game can have everything, though, and GTA 6 is no different. The game takes place in Florida stand-in Leonida but doesn't feature Walt Disney World, for example, but Rockstar says the game will deliver the "full Florida experience." GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game has reportedly already sold close to 6 million copies, generating more than $570 million in pre-sales. Also this week, Rockstar revealed that GTA 6 will have more than 170 animal species, including cane toads and monkeys. We also learned that GTA 6 has a new dynamic weather system.

title: Former Steelers Head Coach Reveals Minecraft City He’s Been Building For 12 Years
description: Mike Tomlin served as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers from 2007-2025, which is a remarkably long tenure in the NFL. During more than half of that time, Tomlin was secretly working on a massive Minecraft city, and he's now revealing it to the general public. In the first episode of his deep dive into the Minecraft city--and the first video on his YouTube channel--Tomlin shared how the city began, initially with his kids' participation, but as they grew older, it became more and more of a focus for him alone. Much like the Steelers' roster changed every season, Tomlin remained the constant. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_h_pQ1-5iQg As you can see in the video, Mike Tomlin put an enormous amount of effort and time into building this city, not only creating the skyscrapers and nearby neighborhoods, but also sports stadiums. He said in the first episode that he'd go into more detail on these stadiums later, but the city includes a baseball field and a soccer pitch, alongside the obvious football field. His son Mayce also shared that Tomlin would sometimes take his PlayStation, presumably due to a sudden creative spark. https://twitter.com/maycetomlin/status/2105457694148821231 Tomlin has a lot more time to focus on Minecraft since resigning as the Steelers' head coach following the 2025 season. During his tenure, the team famously never had a losing season, which might just change this year with a grandfather at quarterback and a defense that has major issues stopping the run. Pittsburgh native Mike McCarthy is the team's new head coach, and it's unclear if he plays Minecraft.

title: PUBG: Black Budget Canceled, Joining Live-Service Graveyard
description: PUBG publisher Krafton has pulled the plug on its extraction shooter spin-off PUBG: Black Budget. Announced less than a year ago and already through several closed alpha tests, the publisher's reasoning for the cancellation is simple: it believes Black Budget simply wasn't fun enough to keep potential players engaged. "After reviewing the project's development status and future direction, we concluded that its current direction would not allow us to deliver an experience players could enjoy over the long term," Krafton wrote in a Steam update. "We have therefore made the difficult decision to end development of PUBG: Black Budget. PUBG Studios will carry what we learned from development and testing into future projects, continuing to listen to players as we explore new gameplay experiences." Black Budget is the second PUBG spin-off to get the axe, following the demise of the tactical shooter PUBG: Blindspot in March. While the game launched in early access, Krafton closed it down after two months, saying it was "no longer able to sustainably provide the level of experience" it set out to deliver. PUBG: Black BudgetKrafton's reasons for cancelling Black Budget aren't without merit. If it had been fully released, Black Budget would likely have faced an uphill battle, as the extraction shooter genre is perceived as a niche market dominated by a handful of games, while the live-service video game graveyard is full of recent projects that failed to find an audience. Many games launch with strong momentum, but they struggle to retain those initial player numbers, and their audiences shrink quickly. Just look at Highguard, as the free-to-play shooter lasted just over a month before it shut down. PUBG franchise director Taeseok Jang recently reflected on the struggles of Highguard and other live-service games, commenting on how hard it is to succeed in that space. Krafton has another PUBG spin-off in the works, the grindhouse-themed multiplayer shooter Ded.Net. Announced back in August during Gamescom, it's currently being developed by Krafton's Wisconsin-based studio PUBG Madison.

description: U.S. markets are the envy of the world because investors trust that whoever owns a share owns it fully, writes Aaron Kaplan, founder of Promethum. The synthetic models cheapens that trust, shortchanges U.S. investors, and undercuts the issuer-led capital markets model.

title: Bitcoin kicks off new quarter in the old $82,000-$85,000 price range
description: Prices briefly topped $85,000 on Wednesday after weaker-than-expected U.S. inflation cooled bets on Fed rate hikes, But bulls couldn’t hold the move and spot ETFs didn’t help.
